digest_convention: content_sha256 hashes full acquired file; source_definition_sha256 hashes LF-joined definition lines with a final LF, including inter-definition blank lines; text_sha256 hashes the complete recommendation YAML line without final LF.
limitations: Source review is limited to the four pinned organization definition files.
Generic candidate extraction does not parse these YAML definitions; independent claims are supplemental and do not establish generic extraction completeness.
Mappings are provisional topical suggestions; no canonical control change or acceptance occurred.
Current platform behavior, API support, evaluator fidelity, licenses and all linked material remain unverified by this partition.
Source-to-control independent omission audit and native validation remain outstanding.

unresolved_decisions.rationale: Explicit tension with org-act-002: local-only is offered as safe there but reported as a low-severity finding here; flexibility is optional rather than mandatory.
Upstream trigger is more than 20 percent inactive seats in the most recent billing cycle; threshold and inactive definition are source-specific, not adopted. Reclamation changes access and cost.
CLI/agent capability wording is pinned source evidence, not independently verified current platform behavior; review product version and actual policy controls.
Upstream productivity superlative is an unsupported value claim; enabling chat is optional and subject to access/data policy.
Signoff is distinct from cryptographic signing and independent review approval; source characterization as approval evidence needs platform verification.
Read/write alternatives are source suggestions; actual least privilege may require a lower base role and explicit per-repository grants.
Publication policy depends on organizational purpose; public/open-source creation can be intentional rather than a security failure.
Security-manager team assignment is an organization role recommendation; accountable solo ownership and product-role availability require an explicit specialization.
Applies only to EMU with delegated identity management; Entra Conditional Access is vendor-specific specialization, not a requirement for every identity provider.

License and product/visibility availability are prerequisites; source description overstates blanket GHAS dependence for code scanning/secret scanning/dependency review and needs official platform reconciliation. No paid activation authorized.

claims.statement: Use read access as the organization workflow-token default.
claims.scope_caveats: Organization default is distinct from workflow root and job overrides; verify effective inherited restrictions and avoid assuming default equals every job scope.

claims.statement: Grant additional write scopes only in workflows that need them.
claims.scope_caveats: Organization default is distinct from workflow root and job overrides; verify effective inherited restrictions and avoid assuming default equals every job scope.

claims.statement: Limit executable Actions to organization-local sources or an explicitly selected trusted set.
claims.scope_caveats: Trust selection needs reviewed publisher/repository criteria; no claim that verified publishers eliminate supply-chain risk.

claims.statement: Evaluate allowing selected trusted third-party Actions when a local-only policy blocks legitimate workflows.
claims.scope_caveats: Explicit tension with org-act-002: local-only is offered as safe there but reported as a low-severity finding here; flexibility is optional rather than mandatory.

claims.statement: Treat remediation of critical dependency findings across affected repositories as urgent.
claims.scope_caveats: Requires complete organization-wide repository and alert inventory; urgency is a source recommendation, with no numerical remediation SLA defined.

claims.statement: Prioritize remediation of high-severity dependency findings across affected repositories.
claims.scope_caveats: Requires full affected-repository coverage; priority relative to critical findings remains risk-dependent.

claims.statement: Review and resolve remaining lower-severity dependency findings across the organization.
claims.scope_caveats: Applies to remaining medium or lower severity findings; review does not require unsafe blind fixes.

claims.statement: Review and address outstanding static-analysis security findings in affected repositories.
claims.scope_caveats: Requires alert access and triage; an alert may be a false positive and is not itself proof of an exploitable vulnerability.

claims.statement: Revoke exposed credentials promptly.
claims.scope_caveats: Credential revocation and rotation are explicitly human/owner-authorized operations; a closed alert alone is not verification of remediation.

claims.statement: Rotate credentials associated with exposure.
claims.scope_caveats: Credential revocation and rotation are explicitly human/owner-authorized operations; a closed alert alone is not verification of remediation.

claims.statement: Close exposure findings only after confirming remediation.
claims.scope_caveats: Credential revocation and rotation are explicitly human/owner-authorized operations; a closed alert alone is not verification of remediation.

claims.statement: Allocate Copilot access to selected active users rather than assigning a seat to every member by default.
claims.scope_caveats: Applies when Copilot is purchased and seat-assignment mode is controllable; universal access may be an intentional funded policy.

claims.statement: Block Copilot suggestions matching public repository code as a mitigation for intellectual-property and attribution risk.
claims.scope_caveats: Filtering is a mitigation, not rights clearance; match detection and current platform policy semantics require authoritative verification.

claims.statement: Review inactive Copilot seat assignments and reclaim unused seats.
claims.scope_caveats: Upstream trigger is more than 20 percent inactive seats in the most recent billing cycle; threshold and inactive definition are source-specific, not adopted. Reclamation changes access and cost.

claims.statement: Review whether organization-wide Copilot terminal and agent capabilities fit the intended security posture.
claims.scope_caveats: CLI/agent capability wording is pinned source evidence, not independently verified current platform behavior; review product version and actual policy controls.

claims.statement: Consider restricting terminal and agent access to teams that need it.
claims.scope_caveats: CLI/agent capability wording is pinned source evidence, not independently verified current platform behavior; review product version and actual policy controls.

claims.statement: Evaluate enabling Copilot chat in developer IDEs to support productivity.
claims.scope_caveats: Upstream productivity superlative is an unsupported value claim; enabling chat is optional and subject to access/data policy.

claims.statement: Include web and mobile Copilot usage in data-governance policy.
claims.scope_caveats: Applies to web/mobile Copilot usage and sensitive-repository contexts; exclusions and feature support require current platform verification.

claims.statement: Review Copilot content exclusions when sensitive repositories exist.
claims.scope_caveats: Applies to web/mobile Copilot usage and sensitive-repository contexts; exclusions and feature support require current platform verification.

claims.statement: Require organization members to use two-factor authentication where GitHub manages their authentication.
claims.scope_caveats: GitHub-managed member authentication only; EMU routes to identity-provider MFA as described by org-sec-006.

claims.statement: Evaluate requiring signoff on commits created through the web interface.
claims.scope_caveats: Signoff is distinct from cryptographic signing and independent review approval; source characterization as approval evidence needs platform verification.

claims.statement: Reduce organization base repository access from administrator to the minimum suitable read or write role.
claims.scope_caveats: Read/write alternatives are source suggestions; actual least privilege may require a lower base role and explicit per-repository grants.

claims.statement: Evaluate restricting member creation of public repositories to authorized owners or administrators.
claims.scope_caveats: Publication policy depends on organizational purpose; public/open-source creation can be intentional rather than a security failure.

claims.statement: Assign a security-manager team accountable for reviewing security configuration and findings.
claims.scope_caveats: Security-manager team assignment is an organization role recommendation; accountable solo ownership and product-role availability require an explicit specialization.

claims.statement: Require multi-factor authentication through the identity provider for Enterprise Managed Users.
claims.scope_caveats: Applies only to EMU with delegated identity management; Entra Conditional Access is vendor-specific specialization, not a requirement for every identity provider.

claims.statement: For Microsoft Entra ID deployments, configure conditional access requiring multi-factor authentication for users.
claims.scope_caveats: Applies only to EMU with delegated identity management; Entra Conditional Access is vendor-specific specialization, not a requirement for every identity provider.

claims.statement: Configure new-repository security defaults to enable dependency-vulnerability alerts.
claims.scope_caveats: New-repository default only; does not prove existing-repository coverage, effective enablement or monitored alerts.

claims.statement: Configure new-repository defaults to enable automated dependency-security update proposals.
claims.scope_caveats: Automatic security update proposals do not authorize automatic merging or prove vulnerabilities are fixed.

claims.statement: Configure new-repository defaults to enable dependency-graph analysis.
claims.scope_caveats: Default dependency graph enablement does not prove complete dependency discovery; language/ecosystem support requires verification.

claims.statement: Configure new-repository defaults to enable secret scanning.
claims.scope_caveats: Default secret scanning does not prove every secret type is detectable or every existing repository is covered.

claims.statement: Configure new-repository defaults to enable secret push protection.
claims.scope_caveats: Push protection is not an absolute block on all secrets; detection scope, bypasses and existing repository coverage remain separate validation obligations.

claims.statement: Enable advanced-security defaults for new repositories when the required license and approved feature scope are available.
claims.scope_caveats: License and product/visibility availability are prerequisites; source description overstates blanket GHAS dependence for code scanning/secret scanning/dependency review and needs official platform reconciliation. No paid activation authorized.

claims.statement: Configure new-repository defaults to provide private vulnerability reporting.
claims.scope_caveats: Private reporting availability and repository visibility must be verified; organization defaults do not establish a functioning response team or existing-repository coverage.
